Model, circulation mathematics, and interpretation

Safety filter

Single-integrator robots: ṗᵢ = uᵢ. The nominal goal velocity is componentwise clipped to ±1/√2 m/s. The QP minimizes squared deviation from the reference, with the same component limits.

hᵢⱼ = ‖pᵢ − pⱼ‖² − 0.6²
Centralized: 2(pᵢ−pⱼ)·(uᵢ−uⱼ) ≥ −2hᵢⱼ
Decentralized: 2(pᵢ−pⱼ)·uᵢ ≥ −hᵢⱼ

The decentralized constraints split responsibility equally between the two endpoints. All relevant pair constraints enter each QP together.

Updates: 0.02 s; goal tolerance: 0.05 m for every robot. Minimum separation metrics account for motion between samples. The little charts display sampled separation.

Circulation reference

eᵢⱼ = (pⱼ − pᵢ) / dᵢⱼ; J(x,y) = (−y,x)
cᵢ = Σⱼ βᵢⱼ J eᵢⱼ
βᵢⱼ = 1.2 max(0,1−dᵢⱼ/2)
× max(0, ĝᵢ·eᵢⱼ) × min(1,‖gᵢ−pᵢ‖/0.3)
referenceᵢ = clipped(gᵢ−pᵢ) + cᵢ

ĝᵢ is the unit direction toward robot i’s goal (zero at the goal). J rotates the neighbor direction by 90° counterclockwise; in a head-on encounter this requests each robot’s own left. The gain uses goal alignment, distance, and a taper near the goal.

The QP can alter this requested motion. With several neighbors, summed circulation need not be tangent to every pair and can cancel. This is a heuristic, not a general convergence guarantee.

What these experiments establish

These are selected open-space cases without obstacles, sensing noise, communication delays, or acceleration constraints. The square speed bounds break rotational invariance. “Stall” means all robot speeds below 0.001 m/s while at least one goal error exceeds 0.05 m.

The centralized 3-robot baseline is unfinished at 30 s but completes at 32.78 s in the separate extension, after a 12.46 s stall. The extension was allowed up to 60 s and stopped at completion. This distinguishes temporary stalling from a permanent deadlock claim.
